manual.title: User manual
manual.intro: modelkeeper catalogs your 3D printing models on your PC and NAS, so you can find them, tag them and keep track of them. The app only reads your model files: it never moves, changes or deletes a file – not even duplicates.

sections.title: Getting started
body: 1. Open the **Folders** tab and click **Add folder…**. Choose a local folder or a NAS path such as \\fritz.nas\…
2. Click **Scan**. modelkeeper lists all model files, computes a fingerprint (hash) of each – including files inside zip, rar and 7z archives – and detects the models from them.
3. Switch to the **Models** tab. Everything that was found is there.

Over the NAS, the first scan can take hours. You can use the app meanwhile. Progress is saved continuously: if you cancel or close the app, the next scan continues where it stopped. After that, only new and changed files are read.
The first folder level below a root folder counts as the creator (e.g. "Atlas Miniatures"). If your folder is organized differently, turn off **First folder level is the creator** for it.

sections.title: Finding models
body: The search field searches names, creators, tags, notes and paths. Results appear while you type; the beginnings of words are enough ("orc war" finds "Orc Warlord").
- **Favorites** shows only your favorites. Make a model a favorite with the star – in the list or in the detail view.

- **Filters** opens more criteria: tag, creator, folder, file type, supports and print status, and checkboxes such as **Untagged**, **Duplicates**, **Only in one place** (no backup on NAS or PC), **Offline**, **Damaged archives**, **Extracted and as archive** (candidates for saving space), **Missing files** and **Only in deactivated folders**.
- **List** and **Grid** switch between a compact list and thumbnails.

Notes in the list: **in 2 locations** means the model is, for example, on the PC and on the NAS. **missing** means files have disappeared since the last scan. **only in a deactivated folder** means its files are in a folder that is no longer scanned.

sections.title: Editing a model
body: Click a model to open the detail view on the right.
- **Name**: use the pencil next to the name. A name you set is kept on every scan.
- **Print status**: not printed, printed successfully, or failed.
- **Supports**: detected from folder and file names (supported, presupported, unsupported). You can set it yourself; **Automatic** leaves it to the detection again.
- **Tags**: type and click **Add**. Dashed tags are suggestions from the folder names – accept with + or dismiss with ✕. Suggestions are never applied on their own.
- **Notes**: saved as soon as you leave the field.
- **Found in** lists all places of the model, **Files** all its files with variant and identical copies. **Show in Explorer** opens the folder (for files inside archives, the archive).

modelkeeper makes thumbnails itself: from an image in the model folder, the preview inside a 3MF file, or rendered from the STL. **Change thumbnail** lets you pick another image of the model, an image of your own (**Choose image…**), or go back with **Back to automatic**.
**3D preview** shows the model in 3D: drag to rotate, right mouse button to pan, mouse wheel to zoom. **Use view as thumbnail** saves the current view as the thumbnail.

sections.title: Several models at once
body: **Ctrl**+click adds single models to the selection, **Shift**+click a whole range. A bar for all selected models then appears at the top:
- add or remove tags,
- add to or remove from the favorites,
- **Merge** into one of the models – when the detection wrongly split one model into several. Tags and notes are kept.
**Clear selection** ends the multiple selection.

sections.title: Correcting the detection
body: modelkeeper suggests what a model is; you decide. Folders with typical part names (Supported, Parts, Base, STL …) and size variants (S_, M_, 32mm, 75mm …) are added to the model above them. An archive starts out as a model of its own.
Under **Correct** in the detail view:
- **Folder above is the model**: everything in the folder above becomes one model.
- **Not a model of its own**: the folder belongs to the model above.
- **Split into subfolders**: every subfolder becomes a model of its own.
- **Split off this location**: one place of a model with several places becomes a model of its own.
- **Undo corrections**: the detection decides on its own again.
Corrections are kept on every new scan. You can extend the lists **Part folders** and **Size variants** under Settings → **Model detection**.

sections.title: Folders and scans
body: - **Live**: local folders are watched; changes are picked up automatically after a short pause.
- **NAS folders** are not watched live but rescanned on a schedule (set under **Settings**). If the NAS is unreachable, all entries stay and are shown as **Offline**.
- **Scan** reads only new and changed files.
- **Full check** reads every file again. It finds damaged or silently changed files and can take long, especially over the NAS.
- **Detect models** applies the detection again without reading files.
Each folder shows numbers on files, size, duplicates, archives and problems. **Problems in the last scan** lists, for example, damaged or password-protected archives.
**Share hashes**: if someone else scans the same folder (e.g. the same NAS), they can **import** your hashes instead of reading everything themselves. Tags, notes and favorites are not included.

sections.title: Deactivating and deleting folders
body: **Deactivate…** takes a folder out of scanning and watching. Everything you entered – tags, notes, favorites, print status, corrections – is kept. Models that only exist there stay visible and are marked. If you add the same folder again later, it is reactivated and everything is linked up again.
Deactivated folders are listed at the bottom of the **Folders** page. There you also find **Delete permanently from the catalog**:
- The dialog shows how many models with your data will have no location left. If the number is above 0, you have to type it. **Look at these models** shows them first.
- A backup is made automatically right before deleting. If it fails, nothing is deleted.
- If the files of such a model show up in a folder again later, it is linked up again automatically.
In both cases, the files on disk are not touched.

sections.title: Backups and restoring
body: modelkeeper backs up the catalog, the settings and the thumbnails you chose into the folder data\backups automatically:
- once a day at start, if something changed since the last backup,
- before every update of the catalog to a new version,
- before a folder is deleted permanently and before file types are changed,
- any time with **Create backup now** (Settings → **Data & backups**).
It keeps the 14 newest daily backups and all others of the last 90 days, and always at least the 3 newest. Every backup is checked after it is written.

**Restoring**: under **Show and restore backups**, choose a backup and click **Restore…**. At the next start, modelkeeper replaces catalog, settings and thumbnails with the backup's state. The current state is saved as a backup first – so you can undo a restore the same way.
If the catalog is damaged at start, modelkeeper stops before anything is written and shows the backups to restore from.

The backups are on the same drive as the app. So from time to time, copy the whole modelkeeper folder to another drive or a cloud folder – preferably while the app is closed. Run modelkeeper on the PC, not on the NAS.

sections.title: Settings
body: - **Language**: German, English, or the system language.
- **Rescan NAS folders automatically**: how often NAS folders are checked. A manual scan resets the timer.
- **Data & backups**: where the data is, create and restore backups.
- **File types**: which files are cataloged. Removing a type drops its entries from the catalog – the files themselves are not touched; a backup is made first.
- **Model detection**: **Part folders** are added to the model above, **Size variants** (e.g. S_Orc, Orc_XL) are recognized as variants. Your corrections are kept.

sections.title: Frequently asked questions
body: **Does modelkeeper change my files?** No. The app only reads model files. It writes only into its own data folder next to modelkeeper.exe.
**I moved a folder – are my tags gone?** No. Moved files are recognized by their hash; tags, notes and status stay with the model once the new place has been scanned.

**What does "2 missing" mean?** These files were not there in the last scan. If you moved them, the note is gone after the new place has been scanned. The **Missing files** filter shows all affected models.
**Where is my data?** In the data folder next to modelkeeper.exe: catalog, settings, thumbnails, backups and a log (modelkeeper.log). **Open data folder** in the settings shows it.
**An archive is marked as broken.** The checksum of a file inside it does not match. Best download it again; modelkeeper does not touch the file itself.
